frames.narration: Customer 3 lives in South. The dimension has one row for them: key 4, South, valid from day 1, still open. Sales made by customer 3 carry surrogate key 4.
Day 250: the source reports that customer 3 moved to East. The record says effective day 150, so it is 100 days late.
The loader hashes region and tier and compares with the stored hash of the current row. They differ, so this is a real change and not a redelivery.
Type 1 would overwrite key 4 with East. That is one cheap UPDATE, but every old sale of customer 3 now reports East, so last quarter's South revenue shrinks.
Type 2 closes the row that was valid on the effective date: key 4 becomes valid from day 1 to day 150. The loader uses day 150, not the arrival day 250.
It inserts a new row: key 13, East, valid from day 150, open. The boundary is shared, so a sale on day 149 matches key 4 and one on day 150 matches key 13, never both.
Seven sales of customer 3 between day 150 and day 250 were loaded earlier and still point at key 4. The loader re-keys them to key 13.
From now on each new sale looks up the version valid on its date. Revenue per region matches what was true when each sale happened, and 8 customers now occupy 15 dimension rows.
